The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, established a responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the Exchange Fund’s investments. The primary guiding principles set the tone for how the HKMA can balance its responsible investment practices with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, which operates under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate‑related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investment activities. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee within the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring all ESG-related work within the office. The ESG Committee reports motions and progress discussed at its quarterly meetings to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and comprising the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi‑annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. Figure 2: The Exchange Fund Investment Office’s responsible investment governance structure. As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office began its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the Exchange Fund’s financial performance. As sustainable development has evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office has re‑examined its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the establishment of a new Business Strategy Division within the Exchange Fund Investment Office, led by the Chief Strategy Officer, to coordinate and lead the office’s strategic development. This division also incorporated the Responsible Investment Working Group—now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team—which was previously part of the Risk Management and Oversight Division. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA’s shift in focus for responsible investment from a risk‑based approach to a more proactive and forward‑looking stance in addressing sustainability‑related matters in investment. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists senior staff in managing ESG and climate‑related risks and opportunities across different investment activities: Public market investments— The Credit, Regulatory, and Oversight Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Team and monitors the ESG status of the fixed‑income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting Active Stewardship" under "Risk Management" on page 40 for details). Private market investments— The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG‑related assessments of each investment proposal made by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks4 posed by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, will affect the long‑term performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The United Nations Environment Programme’s 2023 Emissions Gap Report5 predicts that unless global greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced, the average global temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre‑industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to limit temperature rise could exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded assets. At the same time, increasingly frequent and severe extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investment activities. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate‑related factors in ESG integration. The HKMA’s commitment to the global climate agenda was further demonstrated in 2022 when it set a target for the Exchange Fund’s portfolio to achieve net‑zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three‑pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections will elaborate on the relevant methods. Figure 3: The HKMA’s three‑pronged approach to responsible investment. In pursuing net‑zero goals, the HKMA prefers to engage proactively rather than exclude or divest from its investable assets. First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through a compatible approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess cutting‑edge technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high‑emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding or divesting from relevant investments does not help solve carbon emission problems. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising stewardship, encouraging them to transition to sustainable and low‑carbon operations, thereby driving positive change for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net‑zero investment strategy to pursue transition outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund’s and global net‑zero goals through a comprehensive approach, while adhering to its responsible investment guiding principles. The HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities by integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, thereby promoting climate transition and enhancing the long‑term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA’s responsible investment efforts maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the use of a customized low‑carbon equity index to another portfolio managed by external investment managers. Additionally, the HKMA’s investments in green, social, and sustainable development bonds outperformed their benchmarks, demonstrating the "do well by doing good" philosophy. In private markets, the HKMA actively built a robust long‑term growth portfolio, capitalizing on investment opportunities expected to benefit from long‑term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia‑focused transition investment funds, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia’s climate transition needs. Figure 4: Continued implementation of measures to promote ESG investment. The HKMA has invested in a company that specializes in producing eco‑friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste—including organic matter such as food scraps—and non‑recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on high‑energy, high‑temperature environments to produce plastics, the company has pioneered a low‑temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste‑derived plastic material can serve as a sustainable and versatile alternative to oil‑based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods. At the same time, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting‑edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a strong advocate of the circular economy. The HKMA made two commitments of US$1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019, and further collaborated with the IFC to create a new global climate‑focused investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," in 2021—the world’s first cross‑sector emerging‑market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP program, the HKMA has committed to provide loans for 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors—including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing—in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to IFC reports, the HKMA’s loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in various areas, including economic transition and human resource development. Specifically, projects funded by the HKMA’s loans are expected to reduce approximately 5.6 million tons of CO2‑equivalent greenhouse gas emissions annually, equivalent to the emissions from a typical gasoline car traveling 14 billion miles. A green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like‑minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capacity.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organization and is pursuing multiple strategies to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places emphasis on the physical and mental well-being of its employees and on social responsibility, while striving to advance financial inclusion and enhance the financial literacy of the public. As a responsible organization, the HKMA has established sustainability goals under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for all organizational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee succeeded the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating its vision, strategy, and policies on corporate sustainability and social responsibility. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits progress reports to the Steering Committee on a regular basis. The Green Office Working Group and the Volunteer Service Group provide support for coordinating the organization’s sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ways to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition toward sustainability. Key priorities include implementing carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, such as operating green buildings and data centers, adopting green commuting practices, implementing energy-saving measures, digital tools, and more environmentally friendly work practices, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to use carbon accounting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to employ carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce more environmentally friendly solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programs for the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capabilities, the HKMA has hired a professional team, built a talent pool, and focused on the physical and mental well-being of its employees. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers the use of social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes financial consumer education; and collaborates with the banking industry to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all segments of society. The remainder of this chapter provides details on the above strategies. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats that the HKMA may face in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as more extreme weather causing flooding or other damage, could affect the HKMA’s offices and hinder employee commuting. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plan to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The design of its offices also incorporates various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA’s energy use, air travel, and waste management. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA’s climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across all scopes of its organizational operations—Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel)—by 2050 or sooner. As a near-term emissions reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric cars, and to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or sooner, using 2015 as the baseline year, through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will pursue multiple strategies to minimize Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel) to the extent practicable. The HKMA’s long-term and near-term emissions reduction targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) methodology, which has been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has engaged the HKQAA to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and baseline of the verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing its 2022 Annual Report, the HKMA also published its 2022 Sustainability Report as a standalone document for the first time. The HKMA’s efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognized when it received the ESG Award in the “Public Sector” category of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants’ “Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023.” The HKMA is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel praised the HKMA for meeting high ESG standards, for producing a clear and readable Sustainability Report, and for demonstrating its commitment to transparent and accountable reporting by engaging an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report. In addition, the HKMA received the highest rating of Gold Award in the “Non-profit and Charitable Organizations” category of the Hong Kong Management Association’s “2023 Best Annual Report Awards.” The judging panel praised the HKMA’s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and for making effective use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA’s commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years+ Caring Heart” logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to effectively managing the environmental impact of its operations, and its internal “Green Office Guidelines” provide employees with guidance on resource utilization and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, the HKMA reuses existing furniture and decoration materials wherever possible to reduce waste, and gives priority to the use of environmentally friendly building and decoration materials. The HKMA has consistently followed this approach, and as a result, in 2021 and 2022, it received Gold-level certification from LEED7 and the “BEAM Plus Interior Building Assessment”8 for parts of its office space in Two International Finance Centre that were renovated. The adoption of new technologies and the effective use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remain a key focus for the HKMA. In addition to promoting good practices, such as turning off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of light-emitting diode (LED) lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA’s energy consumption has continued to decline, reaching 2.59 MWh per person in 2023, a 29.7% decrease from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA’s daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions are primarily derived from emissions associated with the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per person, a 45.2% decrease from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardizing equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA has also adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digital work environment to enhance online collaboration within the organization.11 Paperless meetings have become the HKMA’s primary mode of meeting. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, all internal administrative matters are primarily conducted through electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages employees to adopt green and digital work practices, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. At the same time, work is underway to implement an electronic record-keeping system. The above green and digital measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA’s paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a significant 64.8% decrease from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international activities have resumed in physical form following the COVID-19 pandemic, and in order to promote Hong Kong’s position as an international financial center, it is inevitable that HKMA staff will need to travel overseas for work. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees to take direct flights or combine multiple business trips into a single journey when participating in overseas activities, where feasible. At the organizational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participates in the “Gold Standard”12 certified carbon offsetting program to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the program involves waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA’s procurement process takes sustainability and environmental factors into consideration. As part of a comprehensive review of the organization’s procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalized and complies with the environmental specifications of the government’s “Eco-Procurement List,” particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, ESG factors and innovative proposals that contribute to improving productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. In line with the “4R” principle—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help develop targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are provided in the “Performance Summary” section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated directly for the first time in a red packet recycling program organized by the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Employees submitted approximately 3,000 used but still intact red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the Lunar New Year in the following year. Given that the HKMA’s operations and backup data centers account for a major portion of the organization’s overall energy consumption, both data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centers, achieving optimal power usage effectiveness (PUE)13. In 2023, the HKMA’s two data centers received “Gold” and “Platinum” ratings, respectively, under the assessment guidelines “BEAM Plus Existing Data Centers” issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organization in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centers has been a key focus of the Technical Team. To this end, the team adopted green design principles and energy-efficient best practices during the renovation works to reduce PUE and achieve related targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centers’ environmental facilities and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as air flow and temperature settings. As the Technical Team continues to improve the energy performance of the data centers, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green performance of the data centers and develop recommendations to further enhance performance in various areas. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA also began preparing for certification as a “Green Data Center” under the BEAM Plus certification program. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technical Team implemented improvement measures based on the recommendations in the consultant’s report to enhance energy performance and the health elements of the work environment within the data centers.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (the “HKMA”) 2023 environmental data (the “2023 Data”). The 2023 Data comprise total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, GHG emissions from business air travel, paper usage, and the volume of non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills) for 2023, together with the respective intensities of these metrics and the changes relative to 2015 levels. Additionally, the 2023 Data include the volume of food waste generated during that year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level recorded when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling program in November 2022. The HKMA’s GHG emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the “GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023, as well as the corresponding data for the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015, used for annual performance comparison (except for food waste). The verification scope encompassed a total of five office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Two, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase 1, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and a warehouse at 5) Lok Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the HKQAA reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the five assets. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board’s International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information.” The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and reach a conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in line with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included an assessment of internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and the selection of representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: the 2023 Data are materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu-yin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current efforts to mitigate climate change. As global warming intensifies, climate-related risks will become more pronounced, with unpredictable consequences for economies and financial markets. Moreover, heightened geopolitical tensions, increasing fragmentation of the global economic landscape, and lingering concerns over energy security—coupled with uncertain economic prospects—pose even greater challenges for countries seeking to address climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, and particularly in Asia, the challenges of this transition are most acute. As the World Economic Forum has noted, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Consequently, Asia plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve its net-zero emissions goals. As a leading international financial center in Asia, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive the region’s transition. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainable development principles into the core of the financial system. Our efforts focus both on enhancing the financial sector’s capacity to manage climate-related risks and on helping the industry seize emerging opportunities in this area. At the same time, we are leading by example. The HKMA’s sustainable development initiatives encompass four key areas: supporting the banking sector’s transition to net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong’s and Asia’s net-zero transition, yet banks themselves face numerous risks during this process. Under the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and to attain net-zero emissions in their financing activities by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks’ climate risk management, we are also providing guidance on transition planning to help them improve their resilience to transition risks and better manage associated challenges. We are also working with relevant stakeholders to prepare for the alignment of Hong Kong’s sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, with the aim of further enhancing transparency in the industry’s related activities. Additionally, we are enhancing the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy, launched in May last year, by incorporating more sustainable activities, including transition activities. We aim to channel more capital toward sustainable and transition-related projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investment portfolio. However, it also presents opportunities for the Fund to drive growth and generate positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainable impact are compatible and not mutually exclusive. With this in mind, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and have pledged in the "Action Plan" to support Asia’s climate transition through the Fund’s investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for more than 10% of the portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year, leveraging co-investment to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia. Furthermore, in September last year, we released the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise stewardship of assets and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financial intermediation is particularly crucial for accelerating the region’s transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred venue for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers—including provincial and municipal governments in mainland China—Hong Kong plays a vital role in channeling funds to accelerate the region’s transition. The "Action Plan" outlines our vision to develop Hong Kong into the region’s preferred platform for sustainable finance and our goal of fostering sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstrative effect of the "Government Green Bond Program" to drive green bond innovation—including the issuance of the world’s first multi-currency digital bond in February last year—to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to cover transition financing instruments in May last year, and launching the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November last year, we have consistently encouraged regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise the capital needed for decarbonization and transition. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainable development data, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we have pledged in the "Action Plan" to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure and to work toward closing the gap in sustainable finance talent and expertise in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable reporting among small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched a "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional module under the banking professional qualification framework to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Additionally, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we have engaged various stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainable development vision. We have pledged in the "Action Plan" to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, advancing our original commitment by 20 years. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the government’s published roadmap. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement processes. We also continue to enhance work efficiency through digitalization, fostering a culture of sustainable development within the organization and encouraging employees to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of global efforts to address climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in geopolitics have introduced new variables to global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an undeniable reality that is intensifying over time. In the fight against climate change, the current situation leaves no room for complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong’s financial system and, in the process, create opportunities for us. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance sustainable development initiatives and deepen our partnerships with like-minded stakeholders. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we remain committed, as always, to supporting the building of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing our generation. As an international financial center and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across the region and globally. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), which sets out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving our goals, and our expectations for how the industry can work together to advance these efforts. The HKMA plans to strengthen the capacity of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself to address climate change risks and drive Asia's transition to a more sustainable economy by formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory coordination, and improving internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting its influence and contributing to the development of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector's climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness as they transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - Conducting a new round of thematic reviews of banks' climate risk management practices and holding a third round of consultation meetings to assess banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - Finalizing work to incorporate climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's regulator-led stress testing framework; - Continuing efforts to integrate climate considerations into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Undertaking preparatory work to develop relevant regulatory requirements for the local banking industry to implement the climate-related financial risk Pillar 3 disclosure framework to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards; - Completing the development of a new module, GS-2, in the "Supervisory Policy Manual" to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing best practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech with the industry. In addition to its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of a green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy," which provides the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate related financing. The HKMA has commenced work on the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including the addition of transition elements, an increase in green economic activities, and the inclusion of climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will host another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support sustainable financing needs in the region. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," whose expanded scope will include sustainable projects such as social responsibility initiatives. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a model for other potential issuers in the region. Additionally, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also strengthen our outreach efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from mainland China and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyze and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme." Although market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and enterprises is growing, the capacity and readiness of different entities to make such disclosures vary, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with more comprehensive tools related to climate disclosure, including easy-to-use sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be leveraged to make existing resources more user-friendly; and collaborate with major local industry organizations to provide the training needed by the industry. The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, necessitating an expansion of the local talent pool and the filling of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the wider region. The HKMA's key initiatives in 2025 include working with the banking industry to develop professional-level training courses under the "Banking Professional Qualification Framework" for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, and identifying areas where the industry requires further training through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. Additionally, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review the scope of its applicability. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Green Banking Alliance" to launch targeted programs in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier to support the overall economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan," the HKMA will gradually integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting in a pragmatic manner, continuing to advance institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on matters of importance. Additionally, we will conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap" published by the government and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to select data centers for planned upgrade projects in line with energy efficiency and conservation principles. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and improve efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking supervisor, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability-focused organization. The HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of its related strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and working methods. To uphold good corporate governance, the HKMA has developed a sound sustainable development governance structure with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively integrated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts. The HKMA’s sustainable development governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor the HKMA’s work—including its sustainability efforts—and make recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the HKMA’s overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategy and policies at the management level; - With regard to responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the EFIO; and - For other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), co-established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the past years, the Steering Committee was established in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and coordinate more effectively all sustainability efforts across the HKMA’s various functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas: banking, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - Oversee the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA’s various functional departments; - Assess the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Oversee external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. Additionally, we invite Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable finance to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key outcomes and future plans of their respective work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups from the HKMA’s Banking Department, the Infrastructure, Development and Operations Division, the External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-established the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. The Steering Group serves as a cross-agency platform that provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts to address climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, thereby strengthening Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Steering Group, please refer to the chapter “Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system’s capacity to address climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their day-to-day operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a pivotal role in the financial system by channelling funds toward green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risks and accelerating banks’ efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Plan” (“Action Plan”), which sets out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Plan comprises eight objectives across four key areas. To help the industry achieve the relevant banking policy objectives, we have been undertaking the following initiatives. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and to achieving net-zero emissions from their financing activities by 2050 or earlier. All banks are enhancing transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched a public consultation on a draft of Module GS-2, “Transition Planning,” in the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capacity to address the net-zero transition and the associated risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards and the BCBS Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help channel funds toward green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors and is designed to be aligned with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as taxonomies in Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating elements relevant to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable finance. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan set out in 2022 to integrate climate risk into banking supervision processes. To help banks enhance their capacity to manage climate risks, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, which mainly include: - Establishing a robust governance structure that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board and senior management; - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas related to climate-related risk matters: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA hosted a Balanced Supervision Roundtable focused on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and helped inform the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management,” of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control, and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new cohort of banks in implementing Module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management,” of the Supervisory Policy Manual and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to banks’ specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with participation from 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. The results showed that, under various scenarios (including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and macroeconomic downturns), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot programme, participating banks significantly improved their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Recognising that banks face numerous challenges related to data and methodologies in climate risk management, the HKMA has been undertaking various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of data and analytical tools related to physical risk for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on Hong Kong’s residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA is working with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published an application guide and two Compliance Technology Use Case Briefs (in English) outlining technology solutions for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third “FiNETech” event, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore collaboration in green fintech. The HKMA recognises that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impact of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In November, the NGFS published the fifth version of its Long-Term Climate Macro-Financial Scenario, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interplay between transition planning and financial stability for financial and non-financial companies, enabling policymakers to view climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Practical Guidance for Banks on the Use of Green Technology” (in English) to provide financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA has undertaken several applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the broader economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of firms’ environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings of these studies not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, informing relevant policy development. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, such as the HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Centre for Monetary and Financial Research (CMFR), which is responsible for research under the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on firm performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlights its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study is included in the CMFR’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised liquidity backstop arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into its assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this engagement, we help facilitate policy dialogue among international and regional stakeholders on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and incentives, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the HKMA’s Sustainable Finance Action Plan (the “Action Plan”), the HKMA is dedicated to strengthening the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we aim to establish Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, support technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets, enhance sustainable disclosures across the industry, expand the local pool of green talent, and address knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. To establish Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally, catalyse sustainable finance innovation, support high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures, and fill talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region, the Government launched the “Government Green Bond Programme” in 2018 to demonstrate its commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing a total of approximately US$28 billion equivalent in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We have leveraged each issuance to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, thereby setting a benchmark for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the programme’s scope was broadened to include sustainable projects and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (the Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bonds and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent in institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This three-currency issuance covered bonds of varying tenors denominated in Renminbi, US dollars, and euros. The bonds attracted strong participation from a diverse range of investors, with a total subscription amount exceeding US$15 billion equivalent. Notably, the 20- and 30-year Renminbi green bonds were the Government’s first-ever issuances of such tenors, representing the longest-dated Renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date. These issuances provide a new benchmark for the market and further enhance the demonstration effect of the Sustainable Bond Programme. They also enrich the selection of offshore Renminbi investment products available in Hong Kong. Moreover, the strong response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflects their endorsement of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to utilise Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise sustainable development funds, the HKMA continues to implement the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” (the Grant Scheme), launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well-received by the industry; as of the end of 2024, subsidies had been granted for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. The scheme was extended for three years until 2027 in May 2024, and its scope of subsidies was expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The purpose of this extension and expansion is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries across the region to utilise Hong Kong’s transition financing platform to gradually reduce carbon emissions. – Subsidies have been granted for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion (as of the end of 2024). – The scheme has been extended for three years until 2027, and its scope of subsidies has been expanded to include transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving encouraging results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, comprising RMB2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB0.9 billion in social bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People’s Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People’s Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, comprising RMB1 billion in blue bonds and RMB1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuances repeatedly highlight Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable funds between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through these measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in 2024, with a total value of US$43.1 billion for bonds arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024: the world’s first tokenised government green bonds and the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds, respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government’s support for regional market participants in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in the field of green and sustainable finance. The HKMA also launched the “Digital Bond Grant Scheme” in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation in Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance market. The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosures under the Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group) has been actively working on the adoption of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the “Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap,” which provides a clear path for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB standards by 2028 at the latest. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support to entities at different stages of readiness to achieve high-quality sustainable disclosures, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the use of the “Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Private Companies” (the Questionnaire), which was launched in 2022 through a collaboration between the Steering Group and CDP. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainable disclosures by businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable companies to submit their responses online (see QR code below). The HKMA is currently enhancing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, including by identifying core questions within the Questionnaire and providing common use cases. Additionally, we aim to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools available on the Steering Group’s website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its Sustainable Development Report in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains extensive information on the HKMA’s climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as its plans and progress in implementing measures to achieve its climate goals. For details on our sustainable disclosures regarding our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA.” Given the rapidly evolving nature of the sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to address knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local banking professionals’ knowledge and skills in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with The Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (the Institute), launched the foundation level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the “Banking Professional Qualification Framework” in July 2023. The module is designed to help banking professionals acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance more effectively and develop relevant professional competencies. It covers four main areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance, and governance. In addition, the professional level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, targeting mid-to-senior banking professionals responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide banking professionals with the necessary training, the Institute, as the administering body for the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, launched the foundation-level training course for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop a training course for the professional level. To understand the banking industry’s further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently conducting a joint study with the banking industry on “Future Banking Talent 2026–2030,” with the aim of publishing the results in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the “Future Banking Talent 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of this follow-up study will provide important reference points for the industry to develop and adjust talent training strategies and measures, thereby supporting the sustainable development of the banking sector. The HKMA also continues to support the implementation of the Government-funded “Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme” through its collaboration with the Steering Group, which provides subsidies for practitioners, graduates, and students to receive training related to sustainable finance. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the scheme would be extended until 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the “Capacity Building Alliance for Sustainable Investment” (CASI), the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, covering discussions on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Additionally, the HKMA supported the establishment of a local chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that strong financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizing sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise stewardship. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, with long-term value creation," believing that full consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving more attractive risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and systematic manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital toward sustainable investments across different asset classes (Chart 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to fostering the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published its "ESG Expectations" and made this document available to investment partners through an annual ESG workshop and on the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices within the financial industry and among central banks. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to promoting a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and to mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further reinforcing its dedication to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established a responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the management of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The primary guiding principles set the tone for how the HKMA can balance its responsible investment practices with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, which operates under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investment activities. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team within the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee, which operates under the Exchange Fund Investment Office and is chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The ESG Committee reports the motions discussed and progress made at its quarterly meetings to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and comprising the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration efforts and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different types of investment activities: - Public market investments: The Credit, Regulatory, and Oversight Committee, comprising senior executives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models based on input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, see the section "Promoting Active Stewardship" under "Risk Management" on page 39). - Private market investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal made by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks posed by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, will impact the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The United Nations Environment Programme’s "Emissions Gap Report 2024" predicts that global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels unless there is a large-scale, rapid reduction in greenhouse gas emissions worldwide.
